reviews.reason: A explains the operative relationship: drafting is sequential, but the target checks all five prefix positions concurrently in one round, avoiding separate expensive rounds. B says only that the target evaluates the positions, leaving the scheduling contribution unclear. Both preserve the supplied correction rule, 4 ms proposal cost, 20 ms target round, three-token yield, and absence of complete application latency measurements. B's missing operational explanation weakens clarity without making its statements false.

B correctly separates seven final-state successes from four uninterrupted all-stage completions, with baseline counts five and three. A calls seven executions 'uninterrupted three-stage completions' and the seven-of-ten tally a 'trajectory-completion rate,' despite acknowledging three earlier failures and resets. This materially misidentifies the measured event; the reset disclosure and small-sample caveat do not repair it. B makes both events and their comparisons independently interpretable.

B explains nonadjacent logical-to-physical mapping and allocation only when the current block is exhausted, connecting incremental growth to avoiding maximum-length contiguous reservation. A lists blocks, a pool, and a position map but does not explain that allocation relationship. Both correctly report batches of 64 versus 40 at the same 100 ms cap and avoid attributing the result to isolated allocator overhead or arbitrary hardware. A's omission weakens contribution clarity, not factual fidelity.

B correctly locates the halving in optimizer-state storage, 8 to 4 GB, while unchanged other allocations leave total training allocation at 12 rather than 16 GB. A twice attributes a twofold reduction to the complete footprint, contradicting its own totals and the supplied evidence. Both report checkpoint losses of 2.3 versus 2.2 without claiming equivalence. B clearly communicates the resource boundary and observed tradeoff.

Both clearly report 16 versus 24 GB at batch four on one device and checkpoint losses of 2.1 versus 2.2. Each gives the resource and loss findings comparable attention, identifies one run per method, and avoids equivalence, significance, transfer, or production claims. 'Smaller allocation' and 'lowers measured allocation' are legitimate alternative descriptions of the same supplied comparison. Neither has a decisive clarity or calibration advantage.

B states the necessary initialization condition, x_0 in [0,1], and explains preservation through nonnegativity and halving. A says the update 'keeps every iterate in [0,1]' without that consequential condition. Its logged start at 0.8 illustrates only one valid run; the supplied start at three yields 1.5 outside the interval. This is a missing claim condition warranting concern. B makes the invariant's scope explicit rather than relying on the example to supply it.

A distinguishes the kernel's 16-to-8 ms acceleration from the complete request's 112-to-104 ms change, correctly describing an 8 ms end-to-end reduction. B claims 'doubles complete-request inference speed' and 'twofold end-to-end acceleration,' falsely transferring the component result to the request boundary. Reporting both timing values does not resolve that contradiction. Both appropriately avoid concurrent-user throughput claims, but only A calibrates the main result to the measured boundary.

A explicitly conditions the supplied at-least-90% marginal guarantee on exchangeability of calibration and future observations. B states that guarantee without its consequential premise; saying shift behavior is empirically unmeasured does not establish the guarantee's theoretical scope. Both correctly treat 89 covered targets in 100 draws as one realized evaluation, not proof or contradiction, and avoid conditional-coverage claims. B's missing condition warrants concern; A makes the contribution and its limits stand alone.

The paragraphs are identical. Both correctly pair 89 versus 85 exact matches on the same 100-query dataset with slower median query time, 150 versus 120 ms on one device. Each explicitly describes the observed accuracy-time tradeoff and avoids sampling-uncertainty or production guarantees. There is no textual difference supporting a preference.

B explains that each question retains the same answer document and distractors, with distractor order fixed and only answer position changing. This establishes why the 80%, 52%, and 78% contrast diagnoses placement rather than changed evidence content or distractor selection. A accurately reports the scores and scope but leaves that experimental relationship unexplained. Both refrain from identifying an internal neural mechanism. A's omission weakens standalone diagnostic clarity without falsifying its descriptive results.

The supplied proof covers exact-gradient updates on convex objectives under the stipulated step-size rule, not the approximate-gradient implementation. A attributes non-increasing values to that implementation 'under the supplied proof' and calls theory and trajectories descriptions of 'the same update procedure.' That materially misattributes the proof. B explicitly separates the updates and limits the three toy problems' decreases to recorded trajectories, without converting observations into an approximate-gradient guarantee.

Both explain logical-key mapping to nonadjacent physical blocks, mapped access, and sequence extension without copying earlier blocks into contiguous storage. Both distinguish this operation from an unmeasured speed advantage. B includes the supported library version 2.4 and serial logging utility while explicitly separating them from the storage mechanism; A omits those nonessential specifics. That legitimate presentation difference does not impair either paragraph's standalone operation clarity or evidence calibration.
